newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks edge up on mixed earnings response.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks edge up on mixed earnings response.

text.p: Mexican stocks ended marginally ahead on Friday after zigzagging through the session as mixed reactions to first quarter earnings released through the day tussled with changing trends on Wall Street.
"Earnings were generally not very good, but the market took the blow as it had sagged a little earlier in the week, and it also managed to fend off the slump in the Dow," a trader said.
The leading IPC share index ended up 8.91 points, or 0.24 percent, at 3,782.62.
The Dow Jones industrial average, meanwhile, closed down 53.38 points at 6,738.87.
The bourse ended in positive territory after staging a last-minute recovery on buying fuelled by brokers revaluating stocks for portfolio purposes.
"To be honest, I feel there was some window-dressing at the close," a trader said.
Dealers said the IPC mirrored erratic progress by market heavyweight Telmex, which ended flat at 16.44 pesos ($2.08), while its ADRs closed off 1/4 at 41-1/2 in New York trading.
Mexico's two largest financial groups, Bancomer and Banacci, staged a recovery after both reporting positive earnings on Thursday evening.

Bancomer B shares ended up 18 centavos (2 cents) at 2.77 pesos (35 cents) to stand near the head of the prominent gainers' list, and was the most traded stock of the session, accounting for 21 percent of all shares traded.
Banacci meanwhile rebounded 56 centavos (7 cents) to 16.98 pesos ($2.15).
Media group Televisa was a prominent decliner, off 2.50 pesos (32 cents) to 94.50 pesos ($11.97) on what traders said was a continuing reaction to poor earnings.
Trading volume was unremarkable at 81.1 million shares.
On the broad market, 107 stocks changed hands, of which gainers outnumbered decliners by 54 to 30.
